From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call: Model fit + next steps / benchmark links

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion on fraud-detection prompts and the latency/throughput expectations for your checkout flows. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

1) Recommended models to evaluate (initial):
   - redwood/opt-6.7b-qa (fp16) — good precision/latency balance for short QA prompts
   - redwood/gptx-13b-q4_1 — higher quality for the longer contextual prompts you shared
   - redwood/llama-2-7b-quant — low-cost option if throughput is your primary constraint

2) What we'll benchmark for you:
   - Quality on your prompt set (F1 / accuracy on labeled samples you provide)
   - Latency percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99) at target concurrency
   - Throughput (tokens-per-second) and effective token-cost estimates

3) Ask from your side:
   - Can you share the prompt set and a small labeled holdout (5–10% labels) as a JSONL? e.g. acme_prompt_set_v1.jsonl
   - Target p95 latency and target sustained TPS we should optimize for

4) Our next steps:
   - Jonas will share Redwood-verified performance profiles and a short dashboard link with preliminary TPS/latency numbers for the recommended models.
   - We’ll run a dedicated benchmark on your prompt set (non-prod; data isolated) and return a summary PDF and perf dashboard.
   - Recommend a 30-minute follow-up to walk results and pick a model variant + rollout plan.

Links: preliminary dashboard + benchmark docs will be posted here: https://redwood-inference.com/benchmarks/acme-retail-model-fit-20260320

Attachments: I’ll attach a template prompt set and our standard benchmarking checklist — please send the labeled holdout when you can.

Thanks — cc’ing Jonas (SE) and Vivek (CS) so we can coordinate the run.

—
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit + next steps / benchmark links

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful.

We can share a redacted prompt set and a small labeled holdout tomorrow (customer-data redaction done). High level questions before you run the benchmark:

- For the gptx-13b variant, what p95 latency should we expect for short (~50 token) responses at ~100 concurrent requests?
- Are the benchmark runs isolated from other customers? We need assurances on data isolation for regulatory review.

We’d like Redwood to prioritize p95 latency under 250ms for the checkout path if possible — will that be realistic for the higher-quality model?

Also looping in Tom (ops) in case we need to coordinate networking/VPC details later.

Thanks,
Sarah Liu

Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit + next steps / benchmark links

Hi Sarah —

Great question on p95 and isolation. Short answers up front: yes, benchmark runs use isolated tenant compute and we can run the entire evaluation in a private sandbox (no data persistence beyond the run). For your specific ask: at ~100 concurrent requests with ~50-token responses we've observed the following Redwood-verified numbers (your real numbers will vary with prompt conditioning and cache warmness):

Recommended model performance (observed on A100-equivalent cluster, mixed batching):
- redwood/opt-6.7b-qa (fp16)
  - TPS: ~420–480 tokens/sec
  - Latency (50-token response): p50=60ms, p90=120ms, p95=165ms, p99=320ms
- redwood/gptx-13b-q4_1
  - TPS: ~240–280 tokens/sec
  - Latency (50-token response): p50=110ms, p90=210ms, p95=260ms, p99=520ms
- redwood/llama-2-7b-quant
  - TPS: ~600–720 tokens/sec
  - Latency (50-token response): p50=45ms, p90=95ms, p95=140ms, p99=280ms

Notes:
- The gptx-13b variant is higher quality but its p95 (~260ms) is just above your 250ms target in our baseline. We can explore quantized 13B variants or auto-batching policies to bring p95 down; trade-offs: slight quality delta vs cost/perf.
- Caching (prefix / KV caching) helps massively for repeated prompt prefixes (e.g., checkout templates). If your workflows have repeated context we can expect ~15–30% latency reduction on p95.
- All runs are tenant-isolated; we’ll generate a short audit trail for the benchmark run and can provide SOC2-relevant notes for your security team.

Benchmark dashboard (prelim): https://redwood.app/dashboards/benchmarks/abc123
Full report (will produce PDF): https://redwood-inference.com/benchmarks/acme-retail-model-fit-20260320
Prompt-set folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/xyz123-prompt-sets

Proposed immediate action:
1) You share redacted prompt_set + labeled holdout (jsonl)
2) We schedule a 4-hour sandbox benchmark (non-prod) — target window next Tue morning PT
3) Deliverables: summary PDF, perf dashboard, recommended model variant + rollout plan (canary config, batching/cache settings)

If you’d like p95 < 250ms for the higher-quality model we can:
- try q4_0 quant variant + faster kernels (expected p95 ~230–250ms)
- or choose the 7B quant model and augment with a reranker ensemble for edge-case accuracy

Happy to discuss trade-offs on the follow-up call — I’m cc’d and can handle the sandbox run and perf analysis.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
